findings.title: B3 replaced a working tombstone retirement with one the DEPLOYED rules can never answer — every offline delete ends as a permanent, unretireable "the cloud copy may still exist" that masks three real problem rungs
findings.trace: Deployed rules are v2 (README.md:101-107; firestore.rules:7-10 marks v3 a DRAFT and the Wave A deploy is a recorded residual). v2 `allow delete: if … resource.data.ownerUid == request.auth.uid` and `allow read: if … (resource.data.ownerUid == …)` both dereference `resource.data` on a NULL resource for an absent document, so Firestore denies both. Chain: (1) DropStore.swift:613-616 remove() always launches a cloud delete; offline FirestoreAcked times out (FirestoreAcked.swift:94-96) → DropStoreError.ackTimedOut → performCloudDelete spends no attempt (DropStore.swift:772-774) and the tombstone stays, while Firestore's durable queue holds the delete. (2) Back online the queued delete flushes and the doc is really gone. (3) The next refresh's reconcileCloud (DropStore.swift:650-653) issues a FRESH delete at drops/{id} — now an ABSENT doc → v2 denies with permission-denied (a permanent write error, so it reaches the completion) → DropStore.swift:775-790 counts attempts; after 3 refreshes the id moves to unresolvedDeleteIDs, which is persisted (:826-829, :337). (4) The ONLY retirement path is now DropStore.swift:446-461 → FirebaseDropStore.swift:159-171 serverConfirmsAbsent → getDocument(source:.server) on an absent doc → v2 denies → catch → false. Retirement is impossible for every id, forever. The v2 set-difference retirement that used to clear exactly this was deleted in the same round. (5) ProfileScreen.swift:92-101 (added this round as ux-3) then shows "N deletions couldn't finish — the cloud copy may still exist" permanently at rung 2 of the ladder.
findings.harm: A user who deletes a drop while offline (the normal case for an outdoor AR app) is told forever that their deleted content may still be live in the cloud, for a drop that WAS deleted. Because the banner sits at rung 2 of the ProfileScreen ladder (ProfileScreen.swift:92) it permanently displaces rungs 3-8 — localReadWarning (unreadable library), unpushablePendingCount, lastSyncError, upload progress and Synced all become invisible behind a stuck false alarm. Same permanent state for any drop deleted before its first upload acked. Each refresh also burns one billed server read per tombstone that can never succeed. Round 8 both removed the healing path and added the banner, so this is strictly worse than round 7.
findings.fix: Two parts. (a) Make the v3 deploy a hard release gate rather than a Wave A residual, and check the DEPLOYED rules text into the repo (web/firestore.rules.deployed) so web/rules-tests can assert against BOTH files — a green suite against the draft is not evidence about production. (b) Make the client independent of the rules version for this lifecycle: track cloud-acked ids (the save pipeline already knows — DropStore.swift:689 returns the stored form) and skip launchCloudDelete entirely for a drop the server never acked; and add a one-time capability probe at startup (getDocument(source:.server) on a random UUID under drops/) — if it throws permission-denied the deployed rules are v2, so serverConfirmsAbsent is inoperative and the unresolved-delete banner must be relabelled 'cleanup pending' and dropped below the real problem rungs instead of accumulating permanent verdicts.

findings.title: Refusal taxonomy is a deny-list whose fallthrough is the reassuring state: unmapped permanent refusals become eternal "Uploading…" progress; UNAUTHENTICATED is mapped terminal though the SDK classifies it retryable
findings.trace: FirebaseDropStore.swift:189-205 returns non-nil for exactly {3,5,7,9,16} and `default: return nil` for everything else; nil flows to FirebaseDropStore.swift:123 `throw error` → DropStore.swift:738-741 generic catch → the drop STAYS in pendingSyncIDs with only a session-scoped reason string → DropStore.swift:368-370 uploadingCount counts it → ProfileScreen.swift:127-137 renders "Uploading N drops…" indefinitely, and reconcileCloud (DropStore.swift:645-649) re-issues the identical write on every refresh forever. The classification is also inverted relative to the SDK that produces these errors: Firestore's Datastore::IsPermanentError treats CANCELLED/UNKNOWN/DEADLINE_EXCEEDED(4)/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED(8)/INTERNAL(13)/UNAVAILABLE(14)/UNAUTHENTICATED(16) as NON-permanent and retries them internally, so those codes never reach a write completion at all — while ALREADY_EXISTS(6), OUT_OF_RANGE(11), UNIMPLEMENTED(12) and DATA_LOSS(15) DO reach it as permanent and are mapped to nil. FirestoreAcked.swift:48-53 also produces a `.rejected` for an ENCODER failure ('the write was NEVER staged') whose NSError domain is not FirestoreErrorDomain, so FirebaseDropStore.swift:181-183 returns nil for it too — a deterministic, permanent failure reported as progress. Existing lock DropStoreTests.swift:795-804 pins the wrong half.
findings.harm: A drop whose upload the server (or the encoder) permanently refuses with any code outside the five listed — e.g. UNIMPLEMENTED(12) from a Datastore-mode/misconfigured database, DATA_LOSS(15), or a future gRPC code — is retried on every refresh forever while Profile reports "Uploading 1 drop…" and ShareDropSheet.swift:144-150 tells the sender "the link starts working once your drop reaches the cloud". The link never works and no surface ever says so. Symmetrically, if code 16 ever did surface it would issue a permanent terminal verdict (DropStore.swift:728-737, revocable only by a later ack) for a transient token refresh.
findings.fix: Invert the polarity to match binding rule 1 and the SDK's own contract: every error that reaches a Firestore write completion is permanent by construction, so terminalRefusalReason should return a reason for ANY FirestoreErrorDomain code and for any non-Firestore error the seam surfaces (encoder rejections), with an explicit small allow-list of codes to keep pending (only those the SDK could deliver as retryable, if any). Give unmapped codes a generic terminal reason ("The server refused this drop — code N") rather than nil. Drop 16 from the terminal set. Update DropStoreTests.swift:784-804 to assert the new polarity (see test cases).

findings.title: Every drop write is setData(merge: true) with no field mask, so clearing an optional field never reaches the server and the next refresh resurrects the stale value over the local row
findings.trace: FirestoreAcked.swift:32 defaults `merge: true` and FirebaseDropStore.swift:105-108 takes the default. Firestore's merge builds the field mask from the LEAF paths present in the payload, so any omitted leaf is left untouched on the server. GeoDrop's synthesized encoder uses encodeIfPresent for optionals, so a nil `recipientName` / `facingDegrees` / `assetName` is simply absent from the payload and the server keeps the old value. The stale value then flows back: DropStore.swift:414-422 replaces the in-memory row wholesale with the cloud row once the id is no longer pending, and ShareDropSheet is constructed from library.drops (DropsListScreen.swift:91, :99-110 → :20-21) and re-initialises its field from drop.recipientName (ShareDropSheet.swift:20). AccountService.swift:143-146 writes users/{uid} the same way (UserProfile has no optionals today, so only drops are affected).
findings.harm: User re-opens the share sheet for an already-shared drop, clears the "Who is it for?" field and taps Send. Disk and UI show the name cleared; the server keeps it. Within one refresh (pull-to-refresh, tab switch, relaunch) the cleared name is back in library.drops, back in the share sheet, and back in DropSharingService.shareMessage — so a link re-shared to a second person carries the first recipient's name ("left a surprise for Sarah"). Same silent revert for facingDegrees (auto-facing never restores) and assetName. The edit is reported as Synced.
findings.fix: Write drops with merge:false — CloudDrop (FirebaseDropStore.swift:16-27) always carries the complete document, and overwriting a drops/{id} document does not touch its reactions subcollection, so a full set is both correct and safe. If merge must stay for other callers, add an explicit `merge: Bool` at the call site and/or encode cleared optionals as FieldValue.delete() so the field mask includes them. Add an emulator round-trip asserting a cleared field is absent after the second write.

findings.title: state-6 interim fix routes the owner's own link into the OWNER WRITE path: opening your own link overwrites the local row with the fetched copy, re-enqueues a cloud write, and can no longer redeem a tombstone
findings.trace: DropSharingService.swift:59-60 sets receivedViaLink = nil when the fetched ownerUid equals the current uid. RootView.swift:56-69 then calls `library.update(drop, persist: true)` with that copy. In DropLibrary.update (DropStore.swift:559-591) the `drop.receivedViaLink == true` branch at :565-576 is now SKIPPED for own drops, so: (a) :577-581 replaces the in-memory row with the fetched server copy, (b) :584 `local.save(drop)` overwrites the persisted row with it, (c) :590 enqueueCloudSync passes the `receivedViaLink != true` guard at :665 and issues a full re-upload, marking the drop pending (:666), and (d) the redemption that used to clear pendingDeleteIDs/unresolvedDeleteIDs (:573-574) never runs. Note the fetch itself is a cache-satisfiable read: DropSharingService.swift:49-50 uses getDocument() with the DEFAULT source.
findings.harm: (1) Every owner who taps their own link to check it works (the documented invite-page flow) flips a fully-synced drop back to pendingSyncIDs, so Profile shows "Uploading 1 drop…" and ShareDropSheet.swift:144-150 shows "Still uploading — the link starts working once your drop reaches the cloud" for a drop that is already uploaded. (2) If the local row carries an edit that reached disk but was never staged with Firestore — e.g. the drop was created/edited while anonymous sign-in had not attached, so FirebaseDropStore.swift:75-77 threw notSignedIn before any setData — the fetched server copy silently overwrites that edit on disk AND is re-uploaded; pending then clears and the ladder reports Synced over a destroyed edit. (3) An own drop whose delete was refused (unresolvedDeleteIDs) can no longer be redeemed by re-opening its link: it is re-inserted, re-saved and re-uploaded, then suppressed again by the tombstone at DropStore.swift:434-435 on the next refresh — it flickers in and out while its cloud copy is rewritten.
findings.fix: Do not fold the receive path into the owner write path. Have fetchSharedDrop return the ownership relation explicitly (e.g. an enum {ownedByMe, receivedFromOther}) instead of encoding it in receivedViaLink, and in RootView/DropLibrary take an OWN-DROP branch that (i) does not persist the fetched copy over the local row — the local row is already the newer truth for a drop I own — (ii) does not enqueueCloudSync, and (iii) still performs the tombstone redemption (clearPendingDelete/clearUnresolvedDelete + delete-generation bump) that opening a link expresses regardless of who owns it. Also read with source:.server for the receive fetch, or keep the fetched copy in memory only, so a cache-served read can never overwrite disk (binding rule 3).

findings.title: flows-4 only half-fixes the swallowed reaction: the sender listener's order-by-`at` + limit(1) window still drops any queued reaction that is not the newest by the VIEWER's clock
findings.trace: ReactionService.swift:119-120 subscribes with `.order(by: "at", descending: true).limit(to: 1)`. `at` is stamped on the VIEWER's device at send time (ReactionService.swift:16 default `Date()`, used at :56-58). A Firestore limit-1 query only produces a snapshot event when the TOP document changes, so a newly written reaction whose `at` is older than the current top never enters the result set: no documentChanges, no `.added`, and the toast branch at :128-134 is never reached. The round-8 watermark at :124-127 removes the client-clock CUTOFF but not the client-clock ORDERING the query itself depends on.
findings.harm: Viewer A reacts while offline at 10:00; viewer B reacts online at 10:05 and the sender is toasted; A reconnects at 10:10 and A's queued reaction flushes with at=10:00 — it is never the top-1 document, so the sender is never told A reacted. Same swallow for any viewer whose device clock lags the last reaction. The reaction only ever appears in the Memory recap (ReactionService.swift:141-147), which the sender of the drop never opens. The loop's payoff is silently lost for exactly the offline case flows-4 was written to fix.
findings.fix: Stop deriving liveness from a client-stamped ordering window. Either (a) order/limit on a SERVER timestamp (write `at` with FieldValue.serverTimestamp() and order on it — the server stamp is monotonic w.r.t. commit order, which is what a live-arrival watermark means), or (b) keep the client `at` for display but listen on the unbounded (or generously bounded) reaction set and let the primed-set watermark alone decide liveness — the per-listener primed set at :31/:124-127 already handles history correctly, so the limit(1) window buys nothing except the swallow. Also remove listeners for drops that leave the watched set (:114 only ever adds).

findings.title: race()'s no-yield fallthrough still resolves to the GOOD state (.acked) — the one default in the write seam that fabricates a server confirmation
findings.trace: FirestoreAcked.swift:85-91: `for try await _ in ack { return .acked }` then `return Task.isCancelled ? .queuedLocally : .acked`. Reaching the second line means the stream TERMINATED WITHOUT EVER YIELDING and without throwing — i.e. the ack source produced no evidence at all — yet the seam answers with the strongest possible verdict. The seam itself already produces a no-yield finish (FirestoreAcked.swift:48-51 on an encoder throw); that instance is short-circuited at :53 before race is called, so today the branch is unreached, but the shape is one edit away from live. The same file's `delete` path (:61-72) has no such guard.
findings.harm: If the underlying completion block is ever released without firing — SDK teardown (Firestore.terminate()/clearPersistence()/FirebaseApp.delete()), a future caller passing a stream that finishes empty, or a refactor of the setData staging guard — race answers .acked, FirebaseDropStore.swift:110-111 returns the stored form as a server ack, DropStore.swift:690-693 clears pending and any terminal verdict, and ProfileScreen reports "Synced — the server has confirmed your drops" for a write the server never saw. This is the exact failure seam-1 was raised to remove, left standing on the other branch of the same ternary.
findings.fix: One line: `return .queuedLocally` unconditionally after the loop (no evidence ⇒ UNKNOWN ⇒ the caller keeps the item pending and re-checks), or introduce an explicit `sawYield` flag and treat `!sawYield` as .queuedLocally regardless of cancellation. Lock it with the test below.

findings.title: fetchSharedDrop keeps the STRICT envelope decoder that B3 removed from FirebaseDropStore — envelope drift turns a live magic link into "This drop isn't available"
findings.trace: DropSharingService.swift:52-53 declares a local `struct CloudDrop: Codable { var drop: GeoDrop; var ownerUid: String }` with the synthesized (strict) decoder and swallows the failure via `try?` → returns nil → ReceiveScreen.swift:129-133 sets `failed = true` → ReceiveScreen.swift:105-117 renders "This drop isn't available / The link may have expired, or you're offline." This is the same collection and the same envelope field for which FirebaseDropStore.swift:29-42 added a lenient decoder this round, with the stated policy 'old data — local or cloud — always survives an app update'. GeoDrop's own decoder is fully lenient (GeoDrop.swift:104-126), so the ONLY strict key left on the read path is the envelope `ownerUid`.
findings.harm: Any drops row whose envelope ownerUid is absent or renamed — a row written by a build predating the stamp, a future schema revision, or a server-side/Cloud-Function writer — makes every magic link to it dead, and the copy blames the recipient's network or an expired link. The recipient has no recovery. The asymmetry also means the owner's own library (lenient) and the recipient's link fetch (strict) disagree about whether the same document exists.
findings.fix: Hoist the CloudDrop envelope into one shared type used by both FirebaseDropStore and DropSharingService with the lenient decoder (decodeIfPresent + fallbacks), so there is exactly one envelope decode policy for the drops collection. While there, distinguish fetchSharedDrop's three nil causes (Firebase not configured / document absent / undecodable) so ReceiveScreen stops naming causes it did not observe.

findings.title: The 28 assertions never exercise the two read shapes the reaction loop and profile seeding actually issue (reactions LIST, users absent-doc GET) — and validate a file that is not deployed
findings.trace: rules.test.mjs touches reactions only through doc()/setDoc()/deleteDoc()/updateDoc() (:98-144) — there is no getDocs on drops/{id}/reactions, yet the client issues exactly two LIST queries there: ReactionService.swift:117-121 (order by 'at' desc, limit 1 — the sender toast, i.e. the loop's payoff) and ReactionService.swift:143-145 (order by 'at' — the Memory recap). The users block (:146-150) asserts an own-doc write and a foreign-doc read but never a GET on an ABSENT users/{uid}, which is the exact fact AccountService.swift:72-84 keys first-run seeding on (`!snapshot.exists && !snapshot.metadata.isFromCache`). B5 added absence-answering assertions for drops for precisely this reason and did not extend it to users. Separately the suite reads web/firestore.rules (:20), the v3 DRAFT — production runs the v2 rules at README.md:93-115.
findings.harm: Today `allow read: if signedIn()` (firestore.rules:72) and the users rule (firestore.rules:88, which never dereferences resource) happen to permit both, so these are regression locks rather than live bugs. Without them, a future tightening of reactions `read` into `get`-only silently kills every sender toast and every Memory recap with a green suite, and a users rule that starts touching `resource` silently kills first-run profile seeding — the same class of unasserted-rules-semantics gap that produced four findings this wave. And because the suite pins the draft, a green run is not evidence about the rules the client actually meets (see seams-1).
findings.fix: Add three assertions: getDocs(query(collection(stranger,'drops/link-drop/reactions'), orderBy('at','desc'), limit(1))) succeeds; getDocs(query(collection(stranger,'drops/link-drop/reactions'), orderBy('at'))) succeeds; getDoc(doc(owner,`users/${OWNER}`)) on a never-created user doc succeeds. Then check the currently DEPLOYED rules into the repo as web/firestore.rules.deployed and run the whole suite twice — once per rules file — so the suite names, rather than hides, every behavior the client depends on that production does not yet grant.

findings.title: Magic-link receive of your OWN drop routes through the generic update(): silently overwrites a pending local edit with the stale server copy, and no longer retires the tombstone
findings.trace: DropSharingService.fetchSharedDrop (DropSharingService.swift:59-60) now sets `receivedViaLink = nil` when the fetched envelope uid == my uid (round-8 state-6 interim fix). ReceiveScreen.swift:89 `onReveal(drop)` -> RootView.swift:63 `try await library.update(drop, persist: true)`. In DropLibrary.update (DropStore.swift:559-591): (a) the redemption branch at :565 tests `drop.receivedViaLink == true`, which is now FALSE for an owned drop, so deleteGenerations is NOT bumped, the in-flight delete task is NOT cancelled, and clearPendingDelete/clearUnresolvedDelete (:573-574) do NOT run — the tombstone survives; (b) :577-581 writes the fetched server row into `drops` and :584 `local.save(drop)` writes it to disk with NO check of pendingSyncIDs — unlike refresh(), which explicitly protects a pending local edit from a stale cloud row at :420; (c) :590 enqueueCloudSync re-uploads that stale row. Downstream, the next refresh suppresses the id at :434-435 (`for id in pendingDeleteIDs { merged[id] = nil }`), reconcileCloud at :650-653 relaunches the cloud delete, and — because the id is now in BOTH pendingSyncIDs and pendingDeleteIDs — the `.clean` reap at :468-472 sees the row missing from `drops` and calls clearPending(id), abandoning the upload.
findings.harm: Harm A (silent permanent data loss): user edits a drop with poor/absent connectivity (row is in pendingSyncIDs, edit on disk only), then taps their own share link from Messages to check what the recipient sees. fetchSharedDrop returns the PRE-edit server copy; update() overwrites the edited row in memory and on disk, re-uploads the old copy, the ack clears pending, and ProfileScreen reports 'Synced — the server has confirmed your drops'. The edit is gone from every copy with no error anywhere. Harm B (ghost drop + cloud copy destroyed): user deletes a drop while the delete is unacked (offline, or the 10 s ack deadline lapsed on a flaky link — FirestoreAcked.swift:29 — or 3 refusals moved it to unresolvedDeleteIDs), then opens that drop's own link. The drop appears in the library, then vanishes on the very next refresh (tombstone suppression), while the queued/relaunched cloud delete removes the server copy that update() just re-uploaded. Net state: local row on disk, invisible in the app, no cloud row, dead share link, and a pendingSync entry reaped away.
findings.fix: Give DropLibrary an explicit `redeem(_ drop: GeoDrop)` entry point that RootView's receive callback calls instead of `update`, and make link-redemption — not ownership — the trigger. It must: (1) unconditionally bump deleteGenerations[id], cancel deleteTasks[id], clearPendingDelete, clearUnresolvedDelete, reset deleteAttempts (i.e. run DropStore.swift:570-575 regardless of receivedViaLink); (2) refuse to overwrite the local row when `pendingSyncIDs.contains(drop.id)` — the local copy is newer by definition, exactly as refresh() already asserts at :420 — and skip the local.save/enqueue in that case; (3) never leave an id simultaneously in pendingSyncIDs and pendingDeleteIDs. Keep `update()` for editor writes only.

findings.title: A quarantine CAN present as brand-new: the B4 latch's absentFile rule rests on a try?-swallowed journal write, so a failed journal turns an emptied library into an earned "Synced"
findings.trace: writeIncident (DropStore.swift:226-228) is `try? Data(message.utf8).write(to: incidentNoteURL, options: .atomic)` — the failure is discarded and recorded nowhere. In the whole-file quarantine branch (:189-199) the code sets `pendingReadWarning = nil` (:194) and relies entirely on that journal write for durability. lastLoadReadWarning (:236-242) returns the journal, else pendingReadWarning (nil) — so if the journal write failed there is NO warning. On the next load the file is absent (the quarantine moved it), so :145-152 yields `lastOutcome = .absentFile`, `pendingReadWarning = nil`. refresh() then computes `localProvablyClean` at :488-495: `case .absentFile?: return localReadWarning == nil` -> TRUE, and with cloudReadSucceeded the latch fires at :496-497. The reap is correctly gated on `.clean` (:468) so the outbox survives, but ProfileScreen.swift:139-152 falls through every problem rung to 'Synced — the server has confirmed your drops'. The round-4 comment at :106-111 claims the incident is 'journaled durably at the moment of destruction'; the mechanics do not back that claim, and round-8 B4 is the first consumer that converts its absence into a POSITIVE truth claim.
findings.harm: drops.json is unreadable (schema damage, an interrupted restore, a partially-written file from a crash) and is quarantined; the incident write fails for any of the ordinary reasons an iOS file write fails — ENOSPC while the device is at 'Storage Almost Full', or protected-data-unavailable if the load runs before first unlock (the counsel's own recorded residual class). The user's library is now empty. The DropsListScreen incident banner (DropsListScreen.swift:58) never appears, and from the second launch onward Profile states 'Synced — the server has confirmed your drops'. Any drop whose pending entry was already reaped, or that was created before sign-in and never uploaded, is silently and permanently gone while the app makes its strongest positive claim.
findings.fix: Make the destructive verdict survive a failed journal on a second medium and in memory. (1) Change writeIncident to a throwing/Bool call; on failure set `pendingReadWarning = message` instead of nil, so the incident at least survives the process. (2) Mirror the incident into UserDefaults (a separate store with separate failure modes) keyed by the store path, and have lastLoadReadWarning consult journal || defaults || pendingReadWarning. (3) Harden the latch itself: `.absentFile` should earn positive evidence only when NO destructive outcome has been observed and no incident exists in either medium — i.e. treat 'unknown provenance of the absent file' as UNKNOWN per cross-cutting rule 1, not as brand-new.

findings.title: Deleting a never-uploaded drop produces a permanent, false "deletions couldn't finish — the cloud copy may still exist" that masks every lower rung of the honesty ladder
findings.trace: remove() (DropStore.swift:593-616) clears the drop's pending flag at :608 — destroying the only record that it was never server-acked — then unconditionally markPendingDelete(:614) + launchCloudDelete(:615) for any non-received drop. performCloudDelete issues a delete against a document that was never created. Under the CURRENT deployed rules an owner-gated delete of an absent doc denies (resource == null makes `resource.data.ownerUid` error out); the corrected `resource == null` tolerance is only in the undeployed web/firestore.rules:70-71 (Wave A deploy residual). Each refusal spends an attempt at :783-784; at 3 the id moves to unresolvedDeleteIDs (:786-789), which is @Published, persisted to UserDefaults (:826-829), and has exactly two retirement paths: serverConfirmsAbsent (:446-461) — which also returns false under the same undeployed rules (FirebaseDropStore.swift:165-170 catches permission-denied -> false) — and explicit re-receive. Round 6's uid-scoped set-difference would have retired this id (a never-uploaded drop is absent from the query); round 8 deleted that path (:438-445) and added the ux-3 surface, so the state is now both permanent and loudly visible. ProfileScreen.swift:92-102 places it second in the ladder, above localReadWarning, unpushablePendingCount, lastSyncError and uploading.
findings.harm: User creates a drop before anonymous sign-in completes or while offline (FirebaseDropStore.save throws notSignedIn / ackTimedOut, so it never uploads), changes their mind and deletes it. Three reconcile passes later Profile permanently reads '1 deletion couldn't finish — the cloud copy may still exist' for a drop that never had a cloud copy, and because that rung outranks them, a genuine unreadable-store warning, un-pushable pending writes, and cloud read errors are all hidden behind the false alarm for the life of the install. This is the charter's 'reassuring/alarming copy the mechanics cannot back' inverted: a fabricated problem masking real ones.
findings.fix: Track server-acked identity instead of inferring it. Capture `wasNeverAcked = pendingSyncIDs.contains(drop.id)` in remove() BEFORE clearPending(:608) and record those ids in a `neverUploadedDeleteIDs` set. The cloud delete must still be issued (a staged create in Firestore's queue would otherwise resurrect the doc), but for such ids repeated refusals must resolve to 'done' — clearPendingDelete without markUnresolvedDelete — rather than to a user-facing 'the cloud copy may still exist'. Independently, deploying web/firestore.rules v3 (`resource == null` on delete AND get) removes both the refusal and the retirement dead-end; until it deploys, do not surface unresolvedDeleteIDs for ids that were never acked.

findings.title: hasCompletedCleanRefresh survives an account-connection change — evidence earned under the old uid keeps asserting "Synced" for the new one
findings.trace: The latch is set at DropStore.swift:496-497 and is never reset anywhere in the file (grep: the only assignments are the declaration at :313 and :497). Its producing condition is 'a refresh whose cloud read answered', and that read is uid-scoped (FirebaseDropStore.swift:51-56 `whereField("ownerUid", isEqualTo: uid)`), so the proof is a proof about ONE account connection. accountDidChange() (:526-532) revalidates terminal verdicts but leaves the latch alone, and RootView.swift:159-166 runs `await library.refresh(near: nil)` BEFORE accountDidChange() — so from the moment the uid flips to the moment a new cloud read answers, and indefinitely if that read fails, ProfileScreen.swift:146-152 renders 'Synced — the server has confirmed your drops' on evidence from the previous account. This is cross-cutting rule 4: the producing condition disappeared, so the verdict must be revoked.
findings.harm: Anonymous-auth uid changes on reinstall/device restore (the scenario the ownedByAnotherAccount verdict exists for). Immediately after the new uid appears, the user pulls up Profile while offline or on a failing cloud read: the app claims the server has confirmed their drops, when in fact none of the local rows belong to this connection and the new account's cloud state has never been read. The rung is the top of the honesty ladder that B4 exists to protect, and it is the exact moment the user most needs the 'Checking sync status…' answer.
findings.fix: Make the latch uid-scoped. Store `cleanRefreshUid: String?` alongside it and recompute `hasCompletedCleanRefresh` as `cleanRefreshUid == currentUid`, or simplest: add `hasCompletedCleanRefresh = false` as the first statement of accountDidChange(), and reorder RootView.swift:159-166 to call `library.accountDidChange()` before `await library.refresh(near: nil)` so the invalidation lands before the new evidence is gathered.

findings.title: The B1 ownerUid stamp writes the live in-memory row to disk, so a server ack silently persists an uncommitted persist:false edit
findings.trace: performCloudSync's stamp block (DropStore.swift:702-714) takes `var stamped = drops[index]` (:704) and writes the WHOLE row with `try await local.save(stamped)` (:709). By the time this line runs, the generation guard at :690 has already proven no NEWER PERSISTED edit exists: every persisting mutator bumps syncGenerations — add->enqueueCloudSync (:554,:672-673), update(persist:true)->enqueueCloudSync (:590), remove (:605), retrySync (:537) — and any of them would have made the guard return. The ONE mutator that changes `drops[index]` without bumping syncGenerations is `update(_:persist:false)`, which returns at :582 before touching disk. So `drops[index]` can differ from `drop` only by an edit the caller explicitly asked NOT to persist. GeoARSessionManager.swift:1640-1656 calls `library.update(edited, persist: persist)` with `persist = commit`, i.e. persist:false on every intermediate height/scale/rotation slider sample (`liveEditingDrops.insert(id)` at :1608). The code comment at :698-701 defends taking the current row on the grounds that 'a newer edit may already own the row's content' — but the only newer edits that can reach this point are precisely the ones the contract forbids writing.
findings.harm: User drops content and immediately opens the AR height/scale/rotation slider. The cloud ack for the create lands mid-drag (typical: sub-second on wifi, and the drag lasts seconds), and the stamp path writes the arbitrary mid-drag pose to drops.json. If the session then ends without a commit — the user backs out of the editor, the AR sheet is dismissed, the app is backgrounded and killed, or the drop is removed from the scene — the drop reloads at a pose the user never chose and never saved. It also makes `persist: false` a lie for any future caller who relies on it.
findings.fix: Persist server truth, not the live row: `var stamped = drop; stamped.ownerUid = stampedUid; try await local.save(stamped)` — `drop` is exactly the copy that was persisted and uploaded, and the generation guard already proves it is current on disk. Keep the in-memory `drops[index].ownerUid = stampedUid` field assignment (a uid-only mutation is safe against a live drag). Better still, add a targeted `stampOwnerUid(_:on:)` to the DropStore protocol so the local actor does the read-modify-write of that one field under its own isolation.

findings.title: "a backup was kept on this device" / "originals kept on disk" are claimed over try?-swallowed writes, and the next save destroys the only copy
findings.trace: Quarantine: `try? FileManager.default.moveItem(at: fileURL, to: quarantine)` (DropStore.swift:192) discards its failure, then writeIncident tells the user 'Your saved drops couldn't be read — a backup was kept on this device' (:198). If the move failed, the corrupt file is still at fileURL. The very next write goes through save() (:244-253): `loadDrops` re-enters the quarantine branch, returns [] (:199), then :249-251 appends the new drop and `persist(drops)` (:261-266) writes over fileURL with `.atomic` — the unreadable bytes are gone and no sidecar was ever made (preserveUnreadable is called only on the skippedRows path, :168). The skippedRows path has the same shape: `try? data.write(to: sidecar)` (:222) is swallowed while the message promises '(originals kept on disk)' (:170-171), and the next save() likewise rewrites the file without the skipped rows.
findings.harm: A user whose library becomes unreadable is told a backup exists and that recovery is possible, then creates one new drop — which permanently destroys the bytes that held every old drop. The support path the copy promises (send us the backup / we can recover it) does not exist. The 'a backup was kept' claim is exactly the class of reassuring copy the Wave C charter forbids; here it also causes the loss it claims to prevent.
findings.fix: Make the preservation verified before the copy is written: attempt the move/sidecar write with a real `do/catch`; on success write the 'a backup was kept on this device' message, on failure write a different, honest message ('Your saved drops couldn't be read and couldn't be backed up — don't create new drops until you've reached support'). Additionally, refuse to overwrite an unquarantined unreadable file: have persist() bail (throwing to lastPersistError) while `lastOutcome == .quarantinedWholeFile` and the original file still exists at fileURL.

findings.title: The second CloudDrop decoder kept the strict synthesized form B3 removed from the first — schema drift on the receive path reports a live drop as "not available"
findings.trace: B3 replaced FirebaseDropStore.CloudDrop's synthesized decoder with a lenient one (FirebaseDropStore.swift:35-42) precisely because a strict envelope decode made rows silently vanish. DropSharingService.fetchSharedDrop declares its own `struct CloudDrop: Codable { var drop: GeoDrop; var ownerUid: String }` (DropSharingService.swift:52) with the synthesized (strict) decoder, and the result is swallowed by `try?` at :53 -> `return nil`. ReceiveScreen.swift:29-30 renders that nil as the failedView 'This drop isn't available / The link may have expired, or you're offline.'
findings.harm: The first schema change that renames, removes or re-types an envelope key (the same class of change B3 was written to survive) makes every existing share link report 'This drop isn't available' to recipients on the older or newer client, with a message that blames link expiry or the network. The drop is live on the server and readable by the rules; only the decoder refuses it.
findings.fix: Delete the private struct and reuse one lenient envelope type across both call sites — hoist FirebaseDropStore.CloudDrop's decoder into a shared internal `CloudDropEnvelope` (lenient decodeIfPresent on ownerUid/geohash/visibility) and have fetchSharedDrop decode through it, including the same `cloud.drop.ownerUid == nil -> envelope uid` propagation FirebaseDropStore.swift:62-64 performs. Distinguish decode failure from absence in the UI copy.

testCases.name: testOpeningMyOwnLinkNeitherClobbersAPendingEditNorKeepsTheTombstone
testCases.asserts: Two parts, one library. Part A: add(v1) with a GatedCloudStore that acks and stamps uid 'me'; wait for the ack; then setFailAllSaves(.ackTimedOut) and update(v2) so v2 is on disk and in pendingSyncIDs. Simulate the receive path exactly as RootView does — build the server copy `var fetched = v1; fetched.ownerUid = "me"; fetched.receivedViaLink = nil` (what DropSharingService.swift:59-60 produces for an owned drop) — and call the redemption entry point. Assert `library.drops.first{id}.message == "v2"` AND `(try await local.loadDrops()).first{id}.message == "v2"` AND pendingSyncIDs still contains the id. Part B: setFailDelete(.ackTimedOut) for the id, remove(drop), wait for pendingDeleteIDs to contain it, then feed the same owned `fetched` copy through the receive path; assert pendingDeleteIDs and unresolvedDeleteIDs are both empty for the id, `library.drops` contains it after a subsequent `refresh(near: nil)`, and that the id is never in pendingSyncIDs and pendingDeleteIDs simultaneously.
testCases.failsWhen: With the bug present the test calls DropLibrary.update (the only entry point that exists today). Part A fails on the first two assertions: DropStore.swift:577-584 overwrites memory and disk with v1, so both reads return "v1". Part B fails on the tombstone assertions: DropStore.swift:565 tests `receivedViaLink == true`, which is nil for an owned drop, so :573-574 never run — pendingDeleteIDs still contains the id and the post-refresh `drops` does not (suppressed at :434). Both parts pass once redemption is triggered by the link-receive call site rather than by ownership, and the pending-edit guard mirroring :420 is added.

testCases.name: testQuarantineWithAnUnwritableJournalNeverEarnsPositiveEvidence
testCases.asserts: Write invalid JSON to a temp store URL, then make the incident sidecar path unwritable before the first load — create a DIRECTORY at `fileURL.appendingPathExtension("incident")` so `Data.write(to:)` must fail. Run `await library.refresh(near: nil)` twice (the first quarantines, the second sees the absent file, exactly the launch sequence testWholeFileQuarantineWarningSurvivesSubsequentLoads models). Assert `library.hasCompletedCleanRefresh == false` after BOTH passes, and `library.localReadWarning != nil` after the second.
testCases.failsWhen: With the bug present the second refresh sees `.absentFile` with `lastLoadReadWarning() == nil` (the journal write was swallowed at DropStore.swift:227 and pendingReadWarning was nulled at :194), so localProvablyClean is true at :492 and the latch fires at :497 — both assertions fail. It passes only when a failed journal write is retained in memory / mirrored to a second medium, or when `.absentFile` stops being treated as brand-new after an observed destructive outcome. Note the existing testQuarantineAbsenceEarnsNoPositiveEvidence (DropStoreTests.swift:668-687) passes with AND without this bug: it uses a writable journal path, so it never reaches the failing branch.

testCases.name: testNeverUploadedDropsDeletionDoesNotReportAPhantomCloudCopy

Assert `library.unresolvedDeleteIDs.isEmpty` and `library.pendingDeleteIDs.isEmpty` — a delete of something that was never uploaded is finished, not unresolved.
testCases.failsWhen: With the bug present remove() clears the pending flag at DropStore.swift:608 before markPendingDelete at :614, so nothing downstream knows the drop was never acked; the third refusal runs :786-789 and unresolvedDeleteIDs contains the id — the first assertion fails, and (per ProfileScreen.swift:92-102) the user would see the phantom banner. It passes once never-acked ids resolve their tombstone instead of escalating. The existing testRefusedDeleteMovesToUnresolvedAndStillSuppresses (DropStoreTests.swift:493) does NOT cover this: it acks the save first, so its drop genuinely has a cloud copy.

testCases.name: testAccountChangeRevokesTheCleanRefreshEvidence

Then simulate the connection change: `library.accountDidChange()`. Assert `library.hasCompletedCleanRefresh == false` immediately. Then make the cloud read fail (setFailLoads(unavailable)), refresh again, and assert it is STILL false — evidence must be re-earned under the new connection, never inherited.

It passes once the latch is uid-scoped or reset in accountDidChange. The existing testSyncedRequiresPositiveEvidence (DropStoreTests.swift:651-663) passes with and without this bug — it never changes accounts.

testCases.name: testAckStampDoesNotPersistAnUncommittedLiveEdit

Then assert the DISK row's `scale == 1.0` (the committed value) while the IN-MEMORY row's scale is 9.9 and its ownerUid is stamped.
testCases.failsWhen: With the bug present DropStore.swift:704 snapshots `drops[index]` — the 9.9 live-drag row — and :709 writes it wholesale, so the disk assertion reads 9.9 and fails, proving the persist:false contract was broken by the ack. It passes once the stamp writes `drop` (the uploaded/persisted copy) plus the uid, or a uid-only field write. The existing testServerAckPersistsStampedOwnerUid (DropStoreTests.swift:623-644) passes with and without this bug: it never issues a persist:false edit during the parked ack, so it only ever observes drops[index] == drop.

testCases.name: testUnquarantinableFileIsNeverOverwrittenAndIsNotAdvertisedAsBackedUp
testCases.asserts: Write invalid JSON to the store URL, then make the quarantine destination unusable — create a DIRECTORY at `fileURL.appendingPathExtension("corrupt-\(now)")`-shaped path is timestamp-dependent, so instead make the containing directory read-only (chmod 0555) so moveItem must fail. Load once (assert the original bytes are still at fileURL, i.e. the move failed), assert `lastLoadReadWarning()` does NOT contain 'a backup was kept', then attempt `try await store.save(GeoDrop())` and assert it THROWS and that the original unreadable bytes are byte-identical at fileURL afterwards.
testCases.failsWhen: With the bug present the move failure is swallowed at DropStore.swift:192 and the message written at :198 still says 'a backup was kept on this device' — the second assertion fails. The save then succeeds (loadDrops returns [] at :199, persist() at :265 overwrites atomically) and the original bytes are destroyed — the third and fourth assertions fail. It passes once the move is checked with do/catch, the copy is chosen from the verified outcome, and persist() refuses to overwrite an unquarantined unreadable file.

cleanAreas: Refresh generation discipline is complete: refresh() has exactly 6 suspension points (DropStore.swift:390 local load, :397 warning-on-failure, :404 warning, :407 outcome, :414 cloud load, :448 serverConfirmsAbsent) and every one is followed by a `guard refreshGeneration == generation else { return }` (:391, :398, :405, :408, :415 with catch guards at :425/:427, :449). The failure branch honors the same contract as the success branch. I found no unguarded resume.

Save-pipeline generation discipline is sound: enqueueCloudSync bumps before cancelling (:672-674), performCloudSync guards at entry (:684), in the defer (:686), after the save await (:690) and inside every terminal catch (:724, :734, :739). The terminal verdict is never cleared at enqueue time — only by a server ack (:692) — which is cross-cutting rule 4 correctly implemented.

Delete-pipeline generations mirror the save pipeline exactly (:749-751, :759, :761, :767, :782) and the redemption path bumps the generation BEFORE cancelling and clearing (:570-575), so a refusal that resumes after a redemption cannot re-issue the unresolved verdict. DropStoreTests.swift:740-775 drives this with a genuinely parked delete and is not vacuous.

Tombstone retirement is now evidence-shaped: the only retirement is the positive per-document server read (:446-461 / FirebaseDropStore.swift:159-171), which forces `source: .server`, treats every throw as no-proof, and never consults the cache. No set-difference over a narrowed query survives anywhere in refresh(). GatedCloudStore's serverAbsentIDs is deliberately distinct from loadResult (DropStoreTests.swift:838-839), so the counter-case is genuinely exercised.

Reap gating is correct: both the pending reap and the terminal reap run only under `if case .clean = localOutcome` (:468), an absent file reaps nothing, and the pending reap additionally requires `syncTasks[id] == nil`. Set mutation inside `for id in pendingSyncIDs` is safe (Set value semantics / COW copy the iterator holds).

Tombstone suppression covers the WHOLE merged set from BOTH sources (:434-435), so neither a stale cloud row nor a stale local row can resurrect a deleted drop, and the pending-edit guard at :420 correctly prevents a stale cloud read from rolling back an unsynced local edit inside refresh() (the receive path's failure to do the same is lens-1).

The actor-ordering claim at DropStore.swift:699-701 is sound as written for the part that matters: there is no suspension between the `drops[index]` snapshot (:704) and the `local.save` call (:709), and DropLibrary is @MainActor, so MainActor non-reentrancy guarantees the snapshot is current at call time and LocalDropStore's actor isolation serializes the write against every other save. The defect at that site is which value is snapshotted (lens-5), not the isolation reasoning.

ux-6 (acknowledgeReadIncident as a generation-owning mutator), seam-1 (cancellation never fabricates .acked), seam-4 (server-sourced snapshot with no pending writes clears the queued status), flows-4 (per-listener primed set replacing the client-clock watermark) and B6 (retrySync on the persisted drop) are each closed with no residual crack found in this lens.

findings.title: "Synced — the server has confirmed your drops" is earned by a cache-served read (B4's positive evidence is cache-satisfiable)
findings.trace: FirebaseDropStore.loadDrops:54-56 issues `Firestore.firestore().collection("drops").whereField(...).getDocuments()` with no `source:` argument — i.e. GetSource.default, which returns LOCALLY CACHED query results (including an empty snapshot from an empty cache) without throwing when the server is unreachable. DropStore.swift:414-416 treats any non-throwing return as `cloudReadSucceeded = true`; :496-498 then sets `hasCompletedCleanRefresh = true`; ProfileScreen.swift:139-153 falls off the end of the ladder to `Label("Synced — the server has confirmed your drops")`. Contrast the sibling that got this right in the same round: serverConfirmsAbsent (FirebaseDropStore.swift:162-164) uses `getDocument(source: .server)` precisely because the cache may not answer a question about the server. No `isFromCache` check exists anywhere outside AccountService (grep: AccountService.swift:61,73 only).
findings.harm: Fabricated server confirmation. Trigger: airplane mode / captive-portal wifi / revoked anon token, relaunch (Auth.currentUser is persisted, so uid != nil and the ladder's Connecting branch is skipped), open You. Local load is clean, the cloud query is answered from cache, and the app states the server has confirmed the user's drops while no packet left the device. Two concrete escalations: (a) a drop deleted offline sits in pendingDeleteIDs — deliberately outside the ladder — so the app claims server confirmation while the cloud doc, and the magic link to the user's real-world coordinate, is still live and readable by anyone holding it; (b) a fresh install offline has an EMPTY cache, so the query answers [] from cache, local file is absent with no journal (:492), and the app reports 'Synced — the server has confirmed your drops' over a library that has never once contacted the server. This is also the state in which the recorded UserDefaults-outbox residual becomes user-visible harm: if the outbox is unreadable at init (DropStore.swift:355-362), pendingSyncIDs is empty, no 'Uploading' branch outranks, and the fabricated confirmation is the only thing the user sees.
findings.fix: Make cloud-read freshness part of the seam's answer, not an inference from 'did not throw'. Either (a) have FirebaseDropStore.loadDrops call `getDocuments(source: .server)` for the refresh path, or (b) widen the DropStore result to carry provenance (e.g. `struct CloudRead { let drops: [GeoDrop]; let servedFromCache: Bool }`, populated from `snapshot.metadata.isFromCache`) and set `cloudReadSucceeded` only when `!servedFromCache`. A cache-served read must land in the UNKNOWN state ('Checking sync status…'), never the earned one. Same treatment for the copy: 'Synced' must name the moment it was earned (e.g. 'Server-confirmed just now').

findings.title: The Memory's reaction summary counts the viewer's own unflushed reaction — the keepsake contradicts its own QUEUED badge
findings.trace: MemoryScreen.swift:89 `.task { allReactions = await reactions.reactions(for: drop) }` → ReactionService.swift:141-147 `getDocuments()` with no `source:`; Firestore's local view includes the viewer's own PENDING mutation (latency compensation) and, offline, the whole query is served from cache. reactionSummary (:157-160) groups every returned row and renders '❤️ ×1  on this drop' at :63-69, directly beneath the my-reaction line (:55-61) which says 'QUEUED' / 'Sends to X when you're back online' (:165,174). firstReactionLabel (:180-184) then stamps 'FIRST IN n S' off `allReactions.first` — the same unflushed row. The header comment at :154-156 claims the summary 'counts ONLY server-returned reactions'; the mechanism cannot back that claim.
findings.harm: The loop's payoff screen — the one artifact the user keeps — simultaneously tells the viewer their reaction is queued and that it landed on the drop, with a 'FIRST IN 3 S' trophy for a reaction the server has never seen. Trigger: react to a drop with the phone offline (subway, rural, airplane mode) → 10 s ack timeout → delivery = .queued (ReactionSession.swift:73-75) → wrap ends at 15 s → Memory fetches, cache answers with the pending doc. The viewer walks away believing the sender got it; if the write is later refused (rules/quota), nothing on any surface ever corrects the record. Also double-counts in the plain online case: my own delivered reaction appears in both lines, so a solo viewer reads '❤️ ×1' as someone else's response.
findings.fix: Split RITUAL from RECEIPT here too: fetch the recap with `getDocuments(source: .server)` and, on failure, render 'Couldn't load the other reactions' rather than a count; additionally filter `snapshot.documents.filter { !$0.metadata.hasPendingWrites }` and drop the viewer's own uid from the summary (it already has its own line with its true delivery). 'FIRST IN n S' must be gated on a server-sourced, non-pending row.

findings.title: Dismissing the incident banner (ux-6) aborts the in-flight refresh, stranding the library unpublished for the rest of the session
findings.trace: acknowledgeReadIncident:509-511 bumps refreshGeneration as its first act. Every await point in refresh() re-checks it (:391,398,405,408,415,425,427,449) and RETURNS. The banner the user taps (DropsListScreen.swift:58-68 'Dismiss') is published at DropStore.swift:406 — i.e. immediately BEFORE the long cloud read at :414. So the dismissal window is exactly the cloud-read duration, and an abort there returns before `drops = merged` (:436), before the tombstone retirement (:446), before hasCompletedCleanRefresh (:497) and before reconcileCloud() (:499). Unlike every other mutator that bumps the generation (add:545 inserts into drops, update:577 updates it, remove:604 removes from it), this one has no compensating publish. Nothing re-triggers a refresh: RootView.swift:159 is keyed on account.uid (unchanged), so recovery requires the user to hit the Sent-tab toolbar button (DropsListScreen.swift:26) or visit Explore (MapScreen.swift:105).
findings.harm: User launches with a journaled incident, the orange banner appears on Sent, they tap 'Dismiss' within the second or two the cloud read takes. The banner disappears AND the drop list stays empty — 'No drops yet · Pin your first 3D surprise' (DropsListScreen.swift:83-88), the exact cheerful-empty-state-hiding-loss that the C12 banner block exists to prevent, now with the banner gone. Their drops are intact on disk but invisible in Sent, on the Map, and in AR for the whole session; no pending write is re-pushed (reconcileCloud never runs); and Profile sits on 'Checking sync status…' (ProfileScreen.swift:143) indefinitely — the direct answer to 'does checking ever stick forever for a legitimate user': yes, on this path.
findings.fix: The dismissal should not use the refresh generation as its mechanism. Either make acknowledgeReadIncident a pure banner mutator (clear localReadWarning + resolve the journal, no generation bump) and give the in-flight refresh a warning-specific guard (e.g. an `incidentAcknowledgedAt` token compared before re-posting the warning at :406), or have it re-run `await refresh(near: nil)` after the journal resolves. Test coverage below.

findings.title: The ladder makes a definite failure claim from the UNKNOWN state: 'N changes can't upload — the saved copy couldn't be read' before any refresh has read the saved copy
findings.trace: unpushablePendingCount = pendingSyncIDs.count - uploadingCount (DropStore.swift:368-378), and uploadingCount is computed against the PUBLISHED `drops` array, which is assigned only at the very end of refresh() (:436). pendingSyncIDs is restored from UserDefaults in init (:355-356). So from app launch until a refresh completes — and permanently after an aborted one (finding ux-3) — every persisted pending id counts as 'unpushable'. ProfileScreen.swift:112-122 ranks that branch ABOVE the honest unknown state at :139-145, so the app asserts a specific cause ('the saved copy couldn't be read') for a file it has not opened yet. Same root cause on the other tabs: local truth is read at DropStore.swift:390 but withheld from publication until after the cloud round-trip, so a slow network shows 'No drops yet' (DropsListScreen.swift:83) over a perfectly readable library. (Related ordering note in the same ladder: `account.uid == nil` at :78 outranks terminalSyncFailureIDs, unresolvedDeleteIDs and localReadWarning, so a launch where anonymous sign-in fails masks every known problem behind 'Connecting…' — progress copy above problem copy, inverting the ladder's own stated rule at :71-77.)
findings.harm: A user with one queued write opens You during launch (or any time after an ux-3 abort) and is told their saved drop file is unreadable. That is the app's scariest data claim and it is false; the documented user response to 'the saved copy couldn't be read' is to reinstall — which destroys the local JSON store and, for anonymous accounts, the drops with it. The mirrored symptom (empty Sent tab during a slow cloud read) invites the same reaction.
findings.fix: Publish local truth as soon as it is loaded (apply the tombstone suppression to the local set and assign `drops` right after DropStore.swift:392, then merge the cloud rows on top), so no surface ever reasons about an unpublished library. Gate the unpushable-problem branch on `hasCompletedCleanRefresh` so the unknown state cannot produce a definite failure claim, and move the `uid == nil` branch below the three problem branches.

findings.title: The sender has no surface that can show a reaction — limit-1 client-clock window + initial-snapshot skip, with dead counters and a hardcoded 'NOT OPENED YET' behind it
findings.trace: The only sender-side surface is the 4-second toast (RootView.swift:98-123) fed by ReactionService.swift:117-137. Three structural gates: (1) `.order(by: "at", descending: true).limit(to: 1)` at :120 over a CLIENT-stamped `at` (DropReaction.swift:15, `Date()` on the viewer's device) — a reaction queued at 10:00 and flushed at 14:00 never enters the window if another viewer reacted at 12:00; (2) the primed skip at :124-127 discards the initial snapshot wholesale, so anything that landed while the sender's app was not running is history forever; (3) `prefix(10)` at :81-89 caps the watched set at the 10 newest drops. Nothing else exists: `reactionsReceived` and `momentsDelivered` (UserProfile.swift:14-15) are rendered at ProfileScreen.swift:55,60 and are written by NOTHING — no client write, no Cloud Function in the repo (web/ contains only rules, public/index.html and the rules-test harness), so both stats are permanently 0. HomeScreen.swift:187 labels every shared drop '⏳ NOT OPENED YET' from `inMotionDrops` (:58-62 = my non-private drops) — there is no opened/seen field anywhere in the schema (grep across the app: only GeoDrop.receivedViaLink, a local-only viewer flag). Meanwhile the viewer is told 'LIVE · X sees your reactions' (ReactionSession.swift:132) and, on delivery, 'Your reaction reached X' (MemoryScreen.swift:164).
findings.harm: The loop's payoff is silently dropped and both parties are given confident copy about it. Recipient reacts ❤️ while the sender's phone is asleep; the reaction commits to the server; the sender opens the app hours later and sees: no toast (initial snapshot skipped), 'Reactions received 0', and '⏳ NOT OPENED YET' on the very drop that was opened and reacted to. The sender concludes the gift failed — the single most damaging false state for a gifting app — and the recipient was told 'Sent to X'/'reached X'. The limit-1 clock window makes it worse in the exact multi-viewer case the product is built for: on a drop with two recipients, the second reaction can be permanently invisible.
findings.fix: Persist a per-drop last-seen reaction watermark (id + server timestamp) in UserDefaults; on listener attach, evaluate the initial snapshot against it and surface anything newer as a badge/inbox row rather than discarding it. Drop `limit(to: 1)` in favor of `whereField("at", isGreaterThan: watermark)` on a SERVER timestamp (`@ServerTimestamp` on DropReaction.at) so client clock skew and offline flushes cannot hide a document. Until a durable counter exists, either derive 'Reactions received' from the reactions subcollections of my drops or remove the stat rather than render a fabricated 0; and either drop the 'NOT OPENED YET' claim or back it with a real opened-at write from the receive flow.

findings.title: ShareDropSheet's refusal caption outlives the verdict that produced it — the B6 revalidation can succeed while the sheet still says the drop can't upload
findings.trace: sendLink's terminal guard (:186-196) writes `shareError` and fires `library.retrySync(drop)`. retrySync → enqueueCloudSync → performCloudSync, and a server ack clears the terminal verdict (DropStore.swift:690-693 clearTerminal + reason). But `shareError` is plain @State that nothing ever clears except the next successful sendLink (:201). Because it is the FIRST branch of the caption ladder (:130-135) it outranks the pendingSyncIDs and healthy captions, so after a successful revalidation the sheet still reads 'The server refused this drop from this account connection'. This is the mirror of binding rule 4: the copy survives the disappearance of its producing condition.
findings.harm: User taps 'Send the magic link' on a drop with a stale terminal verdict (e.g. issued before an account reconnect). The retry succeeds a second later — the drop is now genuinely uploaded and shareable — but the sheet keeps telling them the server refused it. The rational response is to close the sheet and never share that drop; the gift is silently abandoned. There is no other affordance on this screen that reflects the cleared verdict.
findings.fix: Derive the caption from library state instead of latching it: make the terminal caption `library.terminalSyncFailureIDs.contains(drop.id) ? (library.syncFailureReasons[drop.id] ?? default) : nil`, and reserve `shareError` strictly for local-persist failures (:205), clearing it whenever the drop leaves terminalSyncFailureIDs (an `.onChange(of: library.terminalSyncFailureIDs)`). Optionally show a 'Rechecking with the server…' state while the retry task is in flight so the revalidation is visible rather than silent.

findings.title: A failed profile seed dead-ends the identity surface: 'Setting up…' forever, Edit disabled, and a wrong-cause status that never retires
findings.trace: seedProfile (AccountService.swift:91-125) retries 3× and, on a third rejection, sets `statusText = "Couldn't set up your profile — check your connection"` (:119) — a message produced by a rules/permission REJECTION (offline maps to .queuedLocally at :113, never here), so the stated cause is wrong. seedTask is then nil'd (:82) with no scheduled retry. The listener's retirement clause (:61-65) matches only the queued-profile constant, so this occupant of the shared statusText slot can never be cleared by a later success. Meanwhile ProfileScreen.swift:34-36 renders 'Setting up…' / '@…' and :46 disables the only Edit button on `account.profile == nil`, so the user has no path to create the profile by hand. Same trap when sign-in itself fails (:37): uid stays nil, profile stays nil, the ladder shows 'Connecting…' (:78-81) and Edit is dead — recovery requires killing and relaunching the app, which no copy suggests.
findings.harm: A user whose first launch hits a rules hiccup gets a permanently half-built identity: no display name, no handle, an orange 'check your connection' line that survives a working connection, and a greyed-out Edit button. Downstream, every reaction they send is attributed to 'Someone' (ReactionService.swift:56-58) and the Home greeting has no name — so the person on the other end of the loop can't tell who reacted, while the app shows progress copy ('Setting up…') for a state that will never progress on its own.
findings.fix: Give statusText a producing condition rather than treating it as a free-text slot: model it as an enum case tied to its source and retire the seed-failure case when a decoded profile arrives (extend the :61-65 clause to any profile-scoped status). Surface a retry: enable Edit when profile == nil so updateProfile (:132-159, which already builds a UserProfile from nil) doubles as the manual seed, or add a 'Try again' button next to the status that re-arms seedTask. Fix the cause text — a rejection is not a connection problem.

findings.title: The state-6 fix makes tombstone redemption unreachable: re-opening your OWN link silently re-buries the drop (and gets its re-upload reaped)
findings.trace: DropSharingService.swift:59-60 sets `cloud.drop.receivedViaLink = (cloud.ownerUid == Auth.auth().currentUser?.uid) ? nil : true`. Grep proves this is the ONLY production writer of receivedViaLink==true (all other hits are reads or tests). DropLibrary.update's redemption branch is gated on `drop.receivedViaLink == true` (DropStore.swift:565) — it is the only user-driven retirement of a delete tombstone (comment DropStore.swift:778-781: 'nothing durable may be unretirable'). But a tombstone is only ever CREATED for a drop the app considered its own: remove() takes the early return for received drops at DropStore.swift:613 before markPendingDelete(:614). So after round 8 the two sets intersect only when the uid changed between the delete and the re-receive. For a stable account the redemption branch is dead code. Concrete path: (1) user deletes own drop D; the cloud delete is unanswered/refused → D.id lands in pendingDeleteIDs (DropStore.swift:614) or, after 3 refusals, unresolvedDeleteIDs (DropStore.swift:786-789) — both durable in UserDefaults (:816-834) and both surfaced to the user as recoverable ('the cloud copy may still exist', ProfileScreen.swift:98). (2) The user's natural remedy is to reopen their own link from Messages: RootView.swift:50-53 → ReceiveScreen → DropSharingService.fetchSharedDrop → receivedViaLink = nil (own uid) → RootView.swift:63 library.update(drop, persist: true). (3) DropStore.swift:565 does NOT fire, so pendingDeleteIDs/unresolvedDeleteIDs keep D.id; :577-581 inserts D into `drops`; :584 persists D to disk; :590 enqueueCloudSync re-uploads it. (4) The very next refresh nils it back out at DropStore.swift:434-435 (`for id in pendingDeleteIDs { merged[id] = nil }`) before publishing at :436 — D vanishes from every surface with no banner (pendingDeleteIDs is deliberately absent from the ProfileScreen ladder, ProfileScreen.swift:127-132). (5) Compounding: because D is suppressed from `drops`, the orphan reap at DropStore.swift:468-472 (`for id in pendingSyncIDs where syncTasks[id] == nil && !drops.contains{...}`) clears D's legitimate pending upload as an orphan — the re-upload is silently abandoned. (6) Compounding: reconcileCloud (DropStore.swift:650-653) relaunches launchCloudDelete against the doc step (3) just re-uploaded, so the app races its own upload with its own delete. (7) If the upload lands last, serverConfirmsAbsent (FirebaseDropStore.swift:159-171) returns false forever, so the tombstone can never retire — D is on disk, on the server, and invisible in the app permanently.
findings.harm: User deletes a drop by mistake (or its delete is refused after the ProfileScreen tells them 'the cloud copy may still exist'), reopens their own share link to get it back, watches the AR moment, is told nothing is wrong — and the drop disappears from the Sent tab at the next refresh, permanently, while its row sits on disk and its cloud doc may be deleted out from under a link the user already sent. Trigger: any own-account delete whose cloud ack is unanswered (offline delete, then relaunch online) or refused ≥3× (quota/resource-exhausted, or an absent-doc delete under the not-yet-deployed v3 rules), followed by opening one's own magic link.
findings.fix: Stop overloading receivedViaLink (a viewer-role flag) as the redemption signal. Give DropLibrary an explicit `redeem(_ drop: GeoDrop)` (or `update(_:viaLink: Bool)`) that ReceiveScreen's onReveal always calls for a link-sourced drop, owner or not; it should run the DropStore.swift:566-576 block (bump deleteGeneration, cancel the in-flight delete task, clearPendingDelete, clearUnresolvedDelete, reset deleteAttempts) BEFORE inserting/persisting, and keep receivedViaLink purely for the viewer/owner role decision. Additionally make the tombstone/pending sets mutually exclusive: markPending/enqueueCloudSync for an id still in pendingDeleteIDs or unresolvedDeleteIDs must be rejected or must retire the tombstone, and the DropStore.swift:468-472 reap must skip ids suppressed by a tombstone so it cannot reap a live pending write.

findings.title: Memory recap re-fabricates the receipt through Firestore's cache: an unsent reaction is counted as landed on the saveable keepsake
findings.trace: MemoryScreen.swift:89 `.task { allReactions = await reactions.reactions(for: drop) }` → ReactionService.swift:141-147, a `getDocuments()` with the DEFAULT source and a `try?` that collapses errors to []. Offline, Firestore serves that query from the local cache WITH latency compensation, i.e. it includes the viewer's own queued-but-unflushed reaction document written moments earlier at ReactionService.swift:59-64 (which returned .queuedLocally → ReactionSession.reactionQueued, ReactionSession.swift:72-75). MemoryScreen.swift:63-69 then renders `reactionSummary` (:157-160) as '❤️ ×1 … on this drop', and MemoryScreen.swift:180-184 renders 'FIRST IN n S' for it. This sits directly beneath the my-reaction line that correctly says QUEUED / 'Sends to X when you're back online' (:165,:174) — the same screen simultaneously reports the reaction as not-yet-sent and as present on the drop. B2 removed the hand-built DropReaction fallback but left the cache path, which produces the identical claim. Violates cross-cutting rule 3 (no confirming copy may key on a read the SDK can satisfy locally) — the same defect class B3 removed from the tombstone path.
findings.harm: A viewer who reacts with no signal (the normal case: the app sends you to a physical spot) sees the Memory — the loop's payoff and the only artifact the app offers to save to Photos — assert that their reaction is on the drop, and saves that image. Nothing reached the sender. If the queued write is later rejected (rules/emoji/quota), it never will, and the keepsake is permanently false.
findings.fix: Make the read's provenance part of the result: `reactions(for:) -> (rows: [DropReaction], serverAnswered: Bool)` using getDocuments(source: .server) with an explicit cache fallback, or read `snapshot.metadata.isFromCache`. MemoryScreen must suppress or explicitly label reactionSummary and firstReactionLabel whenever serverAnswered == false (e.g. 'Reactions will appear when you're back online'), and must never include a row whose `metadata.hasPendingWrites` is true. Do not swallow the error with `try?` — an unreachable server is an UNKNOWN state, not zero reactions.

findings.title: Share-refusal retry republishes the PRE-share row, flipping the shared cloud doc back to visibility 'private' and killing a link already sent
findings.trace: ShareDropSheet holds `let drop: GeoDrop` captured once at init (ShareDropSheet.swift:6,18-21) and never re-derived. Tap 1 takes the happy path: ShareDropSheet.swift:200 `try await library.update(sharedDrop)` persists the mutated copy (visibility 'link' + recipientName, :173-178) to disk and to library.drops (DropStore.swift:577-584) and enqueues the upload (:590); the activity sheet opens and the user sends the link. If that upload is then refused terminally (DropStore.swift:728-737 — reachable via ownedByAnotherAccount after an anonymous-uid change, or any gRPC 3/5/7/9/16 refusal), the sheet deliberately stays open (ShareDropSheet.swift:160-166). Tap 2 now takes the guard at :186-196 and calls `library.retrySync(drop)` with the STALE step-0 snapshot: visibility 'private' (GeoDrop.swift:64 default), recipientName nil. retrySync (DropStore.swift:537-539) → enqueueCloudSync (:663-678) → FirebaseDropStore.save writes `visibility: drop.visibility` on the envelope (FirebaseDropStore.swift:91-98) with merge:true. If the retry then acks — which is the entire stated purpose of the round-6/8 revalidation ('a verdict that no longer holds, e.g. after account relinking, can clear') — the server doc's visibility becomes 'private', the terminal verdict is cleared (DropStore.swift:691-693) and every surface reports Synced, while local disk still says 'link'. Under web/firestore.rules `allow get` the recipient now fails the `visibility in ['link','public']` test and gets permission-denied. B6 fixed the mirror-image bug (uploading the unpersisted copy) but left retrySync accepting a caller-held snapshot at all; DropStore.swift:526-532 (accountDidChange) already shows the correct id→row resolution.
findings.harm: The sender is told the share failed, taps send again, is told (later) everything is Synced — and the link they already texted returns 'This drop isn't available. The link may have expired' for the recipient, forever. Local and cloud diverge with no surface reporting it. Trigger: share a drop, hit a terminal refusal while the share sheet is still open, tap Send again, and have the refusal condition clear (account relink / transient permission change).
findings.fix: Change the API so a stale snapshot cannot be republished: `func retrySync(_ id: UUID)` that resolves the row from `drops` (mirroring accountDidChange, DropStore.swift:527-529) and no-ops when the row is absent; ShareDropSheet passes `drop.id`. Independently, ShareDropSheet should read its row from the library (`library.drops.first { $0.id == dropID } ?? drop`) instead of holding a value captured at presentation time, so the caption, the sharedDrop mutation, and the retry all see the persisted truth.

findings.title: Sender toast still keys on the client clock structurally: order(by:'at' desc).limit(1) drops any reaction that commits out of stamp order, so the queued-flush case flows-4 claims to fix still fails
findings.trace: The primed-set watermark is correct (ReactionService.swift:31,124-127) but it can only classify events the query actually raises. ReactionService.swift:117-120 attaches `collection('reactions').order(by: "at", descending: true).limit(to: 1)`, and `at` is the VIEWER's local wall clock at tap time (ReactionService.swift:15, `var at: Date = Date()`), not a commit time. A limit-1 query raises documentChanges only when the top-1 result set changes: a document that commits later but sorts BELOW the current top-1 produces no snapshot event at all. Sequence: viewer A taps offline at 10:00 (write staged, .queuedLocally → ReactionSession .queued, ReactionSession.swift:72-75, viewer told 'Will send when you're back online', ReactionSession.swift:231); viewer B reacts online at 10:05 → sender's listener toasts R_B; viewer A reconnects at 10:10 and Firestore flushes R_A(at=10:00) → the top-1 window is unchanged → no event → the primed check at :124 and the .added filter at :128-131 never run. The same query also silently discards concurrent reactions: when three land in one batch, documentChanges carries one .added (plus a .removed) and the other two are never surfaced. There is no other sender-side surface for reactions anywhere in the app (reactions(for:) is referenced only by MemoryScreen, which is the viewer's screen), so an un-toasted reaction is lost to the sender permanently.
findings.harm: The loop's entire payoff — 'X reacted' — silently never fires for the offline recipient whose reaction flushes after someone else's, and for all but one reaction in any simultaneous burst. The viewer's UI truthfully reported delivery; the sender simply never learns. Trigger: any drop shared to more than one person, or any recipient with a device clock behind another recipient's.
findings.fix: Order on a server-authoritative time, not the client stamp: add `commitAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp()` to DropReaction (rules already pin keys with hasOnly, so web/firestore.rules must add it to the allow-list), and listen with `.order(by: "commitAt")` ascending with no limit — or, keeping limit small, drop limit(1) in favour of `.whereField("commitAt", isGreaterThan: <primed watermark timestamp captured from the initial snapshot>)`. Either way the initial snapshot stays the history watermark and every later commit raises an .added regardless of the viewer's clock. Toast the newest .added and coalesce the rest rather than discarding them.

findings.title: Reaction-listener errors are discarded and the dead registration is never replaced, permanently silencing the sender's toasts
findings.trace: ReactionService.swift:121 `.addSnapshotListener { [weak self] snapshot, _ in` discards the error, and :122-123 `guard let self, let snapshot else { return }` exits silently. Firestore terminates a listener on a permanent error (permission-denied, missing index for the order-by, quota) and never retries it, but the dead ListenerRegistration stays in `listeners[key]` (assigned at :117), so the re-attach guard at :114 (`for drop in mine where listeners[drop.id.uuidString] == nil`) skips it on every subsequent re-key. ReactionService.stop() (:154-158) is the only path that clears the dictionary and is never called from app code (grep: no production call site). Nothing is published, so no surface can report it — while ShareDropSheet and ReactionOverlay.swift:132 keep telling both parties '<sender> sees your reactions'.
findings.harm: One rules/index/quota error on the reactions listener (for example the first deploy where the order-by index is missing, or before the v3 rules land) permanently kills the sender's reaction toasts for that drop for the process lifetime, with no banner, no log surfaced to the user, and no recovery short of force-quitting. The app continues to promise live reactions in the LIVE pill and the share copy.
findings.fix: Take the error: on a non-nil error, remove the entry from `listeners` (and `primedListeners`) so the next listenKey change re-attaches, publish a `@Published private(set) var listenFailure: String?`, and surface it wherever the app promises live reactions. findings.title: Receive screen renders an 'expired link' verdict produced by a cache-satisfiable read, with no retry

findings.harm: The recipient walks to the pinned spot — where signal is worst, which is the app's entire premise — taps the gift link, and is told the gift expired. The drop is intact on the server. There is no retry affordance, so the recipient's next move is to discard the link.
