Capture `wasNeverAcked = pendingSyncIDs.contains(drop.id)` in remove() BEFORE clearPending(:608) and record it durably; for such ids, bounded refusals resolve to done (clearPendingDelete, no unresolved verdict, no user-facing claim about a cloud copy). Better still, make 'server has seen this id' a first-class durable fact (ackedCloudIDs) rather than something inferred from the outbox — that single fact closes lens-3, half of seams-1, and removes the guesswork from the ladder. Deploying v3 removes the refusal at the source and should be the release gate regardless.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified by grep: hasCompletedCleanRefresh is assigned in exactly two places — the declaration (DropStore.swift:313) and :497. accountDidChange (:526-532) only re-enqueues terminal ids. The evidence the latch encodes is uid-scoped by construction (FirebaseDropStore.swift:51-56 filters ownerUid == the CURRENT uid), so its producing condition disappears when the uid changes — binding rule 4 says the verdict must be revoked. RootView.swift:159-166 makes it worse by ordering `await library.refresh(near: nil)` BEFORE library.accountDidChange(), so even a corrected accountDidChange would land after the new evidence was gathered. Trigger (anonymous uid change on reinstall/restore) is the same scenario the ownedByAnotherAccount verdict exists to serve, so it is not hypothetical.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Scope the evidence to what produced it: store `cleanRefreshUid: String?` beside the latch and compute hasCompletedCleanRefresh as `cleanRefreshUid == currentUid`; at minimum set the latch false as the first statement of accountDidChange() and reorder RootView.swift:159-166 to invalidate before refreshing. The general rule worth writing into the codebase: every cached positive claim carries the identity of the connection that earned it.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified both ends. DropStore.swift:702-714 snapshots `var stamped = drops[index]` (:704) and writes the WHOLE row with local.save(stamped) (:709). The generation guard at :690 proves no newer PERSISTED edit exists, because every persisting mutator bumps syncGenerations — but update(_:persist:false) returns at :582 before touching disk and never bumps, so drops[index] can differ from `drop` exactly by an edit the caller asked not to persist. The live producer is real: GeoARSessionManager.swift:1595-1660 calls `library.update(edited, persist: persist)` with persist = commit on every intermediate height/scale/rotation sample (liveEditingDrops.insert at :1609). An ack landing mid-drag therefore writes an uncommitted pose to disk; the most plausible trigger is a drop created offline whose reconcile acks while the user is adjusting it at the spot. The code comment at :698-701 defends the choice on the grounds that a newer edit may own the row — but the only newer edits reachable there are precisely the ones the contract forbids writing.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Persist server truth, not the live row: `var stamped = drop; stamped.ownerUid = stampedUid; try await local.save(stamped)` — `drop` is the copy that was persisted and uploaded and the generation guard already proves it is current on disk — while keeping the field-only in-memory assignment. The cleaner form is a targeted `stampOwnerUid(_:on:)` on the DropStore protocol so the local actor does the read-modify-write of that single field under its own isolation, which also removes the whole-file rewrite from an ack path (see own-1).

verdicts.reasoning: Verified: DropStore.swift:192 `try? FileManager.default.moveItem` discards its failure, then :198 writes the user-facing claim 'a backup was kept on this device' unconditionally; preserveUnreadable (:217-224) is called only on the skippedRows path (:168), so the whole-file case has no sidecar at all, and its own write at :222 is likewise `try?` while the message at :170-171 promises 'originals kept on disk'. The destruction path is real: if the move failed the bad bytes remain at fileURL, the next save() re-enters loadDrops (which returns [] at :199 rather than throwing), appends, and persist() (:261-266) atomically overwrites the only copy. The charter forbids exactly this class — reassuring copy the mechanics cannot back — and here the copy also names a recovery that does not exist.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Choose the copy from the verified outcome, not from the intent: do/catch the move and the sidecar write, emit 'a backup was kept on this device' only on success and an explicit 'couldn't be read and couldn't be backed up' otherwise. Then make the invariant structural: persist() must refuse to write while lastOutcome == .quarantinedWholeFile and unreadable bytes still exist at fileURL (surface it through lastPersistError), so the app can never destroy evidence it has just told the user it kept.

verdicts.reasoning: Duplicate of seams-7 from the state-machine lens; same trace (DropSharingService.swift:52-53 strict envelope vs FirebaseDropStore.swift:35-42 lenient), same conclusion. LOW: no current writer of drops/{id} omits the envelope ownerUid, so the harm is a future-schema hazard rather than a live outage. Correctly identified as an asymmetry that contradicts B3's own stated policy.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Same as seams-7 — one shared lenient CloudDropEnvelope for the collection, plus distinguishing decode failure from absence in the receive UI. Merge the two findings when scheduling.

verdicts.reasoning: The charter-defining defect of the round. FirebaseDropStore.swift:54-56 issues getDocuments() with no source, i.e. GetSource.default, documented as 'try to retrieve an up-to-date (server-retrieved) snapshot, but fall back to returning cached data if the server can't be reached'. For QUERIES the offline resolution is a cache-served snapshot with metadata.isFromCache == true and no throw — including an empty snapshot from an empty cache. DropStore.swift:414-416 treats any non-throwing return as cloudReadSucceeded, :496-498 earns the latch, ProfileScreen.swift:146-152 prints 'Synced — the server has confirmed your drops' with no packet having left the device. The contrast within the same file is decisive: serverConfirmsAbsent (FirebaseDropStore.swift:162-164) forces source:.server precisely because the cache may not answer a question about the server. Grep confirms isFromCache is checked nowhere outside AccountService.swift:61,73. Escalation (a) is confirmed and is the sharpest harm: pendingDeleteIDs is deliberately absent from the ladder (ProfileScreen.swift:127-132), so a drop deleted offline whose cloud doc and magic link are still live is reported as server-confirmed. Escalation (b) is REFUTED: on a fresh install offline anonymous sign-in cannot complete, so account.uid is nil and the ladder stops at 'Connecting…' (ProfileScreen.swift:78-81); the reachable variant is a RELAUNCH offline, where Auth restores currentUser from the keychain without network. The vacuity note on the existing B4 tests is correct — GatedCloudStore has no cache concept, so no round-8 test can distinguish 'the cloud answered' from 'the cache answered'.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Carry provenance through the seam rather than inferring health from the absence of a throw: widen the cloud read to `struct CloudRead { let drops: [GeoDrop]; let servedFromCache: Bool }` populated from snapshot.metadata.isFromCache, and set cloudReadSucceeded only when !servedFromCache. Prefer this over forcing source:.server for the refresh path — .server would make offline refreshes throw and degrade the offline library, whereas provenance gates only the CLAIM. A cache-served read must land in 'Checking sync status…', never the earned state, and the earned copy should name its moment ('Server-confirmed just now'). Extend GatedCloudStore with a servedFromCache flag so the B4 tests stop being vacuous.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified: MemoryScreen.swift:89 fetches via ReactionService.swift:141-147, a getDocuments() with the default source and a `try?` that collapses errors to []. Firestore's documented latency compensation means every snapshot — cached OR server-raised — reflects the local mutation queue, with metadata.hasPendingWrites true on the affected documents, so an unacked reaction appears in the recap even online, not just offline. MemoryScreen.swift:157-160 groups every returned row with no uid or pending filter, :63-69 renders '❤️ ×1 on this drop' directly beneath the my-reaction line that says QUEUED / 'Sends to X when you're back online' (:165,:174), and :180-184 stamps 'FIRST IN n S' off the same row. The header comment at :154-156 claiming the summary counts only server-returned reactions is unsupported by the mechanism. B2 removed the fabricated DropReaction and left an equivalent fabrication one layer down, on the only artifact the app invites the user to keep (:75, :197-201). Merged with flows-2.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Return provenance and pending state from the recap read: `reactions(for:) -> (rows: [DropReaction], serverAnswered: Bool)` using getDocuments(source:.server) with an explicit cache fallback, or read snapshot.metadata.isFromCache and filter rows with metadata.hasPendingWrites. Exclude the viewer's own uid from the summary (it already has its own line with its true delivery) and gate 'FIRST IN n S' on a server-sourced non-pending row. Stop swallowing the error with `try?` — an unreachable server is UNKNOWN ('Reactions will appear when you're back online'), not zero.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified mechanism: acknowledgeReadIncident bumps refreshGeneration as its first act (DropStore.swift:509-511), and every await in refresh() returns on a generation mismatch (:391,398,405,408,415,425,427,449). The dismissible banner is published at :406, immediately before the long cloud read at :414, so a dismissal landing in that window returns before `drops = merged` (:436), before tombstone retirement (:446), before the latch (:497) and before reconcileCloud() (:499). Unlike every other generation-bumping mutator (add:545, update:577, remove:604) this one publishes nothing of its own, and nothing re-triggers a refresh: the app-level triggers are AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:34 (launch), RootView.swift:159 (keyed on account.uid, unchanged), DropsListScreen.swift:26 (toolbar) and MapScreen.swift:106 (Explore). So the library stays unpublished and the outbox unflushed until the user happens to hit one of those. I calibrate severity below the reviewer's HIGH only because the precondition — a journaled read incident — is itself rare; when it does occur the consequence is exactly the cheerful-empty-state the C12 banner block exists to prevent, now with the banner gone. Round 8 (ux-6) introduced the generation bump, so this is a fix that created a new failure.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Separate the two concerns: make acknowledgeReadIncident a pure banner mutator (clear localReadWarning, resolve the journal) and give the in-flight refresh a warning-specific token to compare before re-posting at :406, so a dismissal cannot invalidate unrelated work. If the generation bump is kept for its ordering guarantee, it must be paired with a re-run (`await refresh(near: nil)` after the journal resolves). General rule: a generation bump is a promise that the mutator publishes newer state — a mutator that publishes nothing must not use it.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified: unpushablePendingCount = pendingSyncIDs.count - uploadingCount (DropStore.swift:368-378) and uploadingCount filters against the PUBLISHED drops array, which is assigned only at :436 — the end of refresh, after the cloud round-trip. pendingSyncIDs is restored from UserDefaults in init (:355-356). So from launch until the first refresh completes (and permanently after any aborted refresh, ux-3 or own-2), every persisted pending id is reported as unpushable, and ProfileScreen.swift:112-122 ranks that definite failure claim ABOVE the honest unknown at :139-145. The claim it makes — 'the saved copy couldn't be read' — is the app's scariest data statement and the documented user response to it (reinstall) destroys the local JSON store, which for anonymous accounts is the only copy of any never-uploaded drop. The parenthetical ordering note is also correct: ProfileScreen.swift:78 puts `account.uid == nil` above terminal verdicts, unresolved deletes and localReadWarning, so a failed sign-in masks known problems behind progress copy, inverting the ladder's own stated rule. The vacuity note on DropStoreTests.swift:717 holds — it samples only after a completed refresh.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Two-phase publish: assign `drops` from the tombstone-suppressed LOCAL set immediately after the local load (DropStore.swift:392) and merge cloud rows on top at :436, so no surface ever reasons about an unpublished library and a slow network can never show 'No drops yet' over a readable store. Then gate every definite-cause branch on hasCompletedCleanRefresh — the unknown state may not produce a specific diagnosis — and move the uid == nil branch below the three problem branches. This is the same fix as own-2.

verdicts.reasoning: Every component verified. (1) The limit-1 client-clock window is the same defect as seams-5/flows-4. (2) The primed skip at ReactionService.swift:124-127 discards the whole initial snapshot, so anything that landed while the sender's app was not running is history forever — and since the listener is only attached from RootView.swift:152-154 while the app is foreground, that is the normal case for a gift opened hours later. (3) The counters are dead: grep shows momentsDelivered/reactionsReceived (UserProfile.swift:14-15) are read at ProfileScreen.swift:55,60 and written by nothing — no client write, and web/ contains only firestore.rules, public/index.html and rules-tests, so there is no Cloud Function to write them; both render a permanent 0. (4) HomeScreen.swift:187 prints '⏳ NOT OPENED YET' for every non-private owned drop (:58-62) with no opened/seen field anywhere in the schema. So the sender's three surfaces jointly assert the gift was never opened while the recipient was told 'Sent to X' (MemoryScreen.swift:164) and 'LIVE · X sees your reactions'. For a gifting app this is the single most damaging false state.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Persist a per-drop last-seen watermark (reaction id + server timestamp) and evaluate the INITIAL snapshot against it on attach — surface anything newer as a badge or inbox row instead of discarding it; that also removes the need for limit(1). Pair with the server-timestamp ordering from seams-5. For the counters: either derive 'Reactions received' client-side from the reactions subcollections of my drops, or remove the stat until a durable writer exists — a fabricated 0 is worse than no tile. Either drop the 'NOT OPENED YET' claim or back it with a real opened-at write from the receive flow (which the rules already permit for the drop owner's own document).

verdicts.reasoning: Verified: shareError is plain @State (ShareDropSheet.swift:16), written by the terminal guard at :187, and cleared only by a subsequent successful sendLink at :201. It is the FIRST branch of the caption ladder (:130-135), so it outranks the live library-derived captions at :135-155. Since the same guard fires library.retrySync(drop) at :194 and a server ack clears the terminal verdict (DropStore.swift:690-693), the sheet can keep asserting 'The server refused this drop from this account connection' for a drop that is now genuinely uploaded — binding rule 4 inverted, copy outliving its producing condition. Severity is bounded by the fact that a second tap now takes the happy path and clears it, so the user has a (silent, undiscoverable) way out; the realistic harm is abandonment of the share.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Derive the caption from library state, never latch it: `library.terminalSyncFailureIDs.contains(drop.id) ? (library.syncFailureReasons[drop.id] ?? default) : nil`, reserving shareError strictly for the local-persist failure at :205 and clearing it on .onChange(of: library.terminalSyncFailureIDs). Show an explicit 'Rechecking with the server…' state while the revalidation task is in flight so the retry is visible rather than silent.

verdicts.reasoning: Two of three claims hold; the dead-end claim is overstated. CONFIRMED: seedProfile's third rejection sets statusText = 'Couldn't set up your profile — check your connection' (AccountService.swift:119) for a condition that is by construction NOT a connection problem — offline maps to .queuedLocally at :112-115, so reaching :116 means the server ANSWERED and refused; and the listener's retirement clause (:61-65) matches only the queued constant, so this occupant of the shared slot is never retired by a later success. CONFIRMED: ProfileScreen.swift:34-36 shows 'Setting up…'/'@…' and :46 hard-disables the only Edit button on profile == nil, so there is no manual path to create a profile, and every reaction the user sends is attributed to 'Someone' (ReactionService.swift:56-58). REFUTED as stated: 'no scheduled retry / requires killing the app' — seedTask is nilled at :82-83, and the listener is registered with includeMetadataChanges (:51), so any subsequent server-sourced !exists snapshot (e.g. after a reconnect) re-arms the seed within the same session, and start() re-attaches on every launch. So the state is recoverable; what is not recoverable is the stale wrong-cause status text.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Give statusText a producing condition instead of treating it as a free-text slot: model it as an enum case tagged with its source and retire any profile-scoped case when a decoded profile arrives (widen the :61-65 clause). Fix the cause text — a rules rejection is not a connection problem. And provide agency: enable Edit when profile == nil so updateProfile (:132-159, which already constructs a UserProfile from nil) doubles as a manual seed, or add an explicit 'Try again' next to the status. Cloud-Function seeding remains the recorded structural answer.

verdicts.reasoning: Same family as lens-1/seams-4 and the trace adds two consequences the others miss, both verified. (i) Grep confirms DropSharingService.swift:59-60 is the ONLY production writer of receivedViaLink == true, and a tombstone is only ever created for a drop the app considers its own (remove() early-returns for received drops at :613 before markPendingDelete), so after round 8 the redemption branch at :565 is dead code for a stable account — the two sets intersect only across a uid change. (ii) The reap at :468-472 clears the re-upload as an orphan because the row is suppressed from `drops` at :434-435, and reconcileCloud at :650-653 relaunches the delete against the document the receive path just re-uploaded, so the app races its own upload against its own delete. verdicts.industrialSolution: Same single fix as lens-1/seams-4 (explicit redeem entry point, redemption keyed on link-receipt not ownership, pending-edit protection, mutually exclusive pending/tombstone sets, reap skips tombstone-suppressed ids). Add the invariant as an assertion in markPending/markPendingDelete so a future caller cannot recreate the overlap, and rewrite the two redemption tests to drive the value DropSharingService actually produces.

verdicts.reasoning: Identical mechanism to ux-2, independently traced (ReactionService.swift:141-147 default-source getDocuments with `try?`, MemoryScreen.swift:63-69/:157-160/:180-184). The cache-as-evidence framing is the right one: this is the same class binding rule 3 forbids and the same class B3 removed from the tombstone path in this very round, left standing on the reaction path. One refinement: this is not offline-only — Firestore's documented latency compensation means the viewer's own unacked write is included in any snapshot, with hasPendingWrites set, so the fabricated count also occurs online whenever the ack has not yet landed (the .queued state the pill is showing).
verdicts.industrialSolution: As ux-2: provenance plus pending-write filtering plus own-uid exclusion, error surfaced as UNKNOWN rather than zero. Schedule as one change with ux-2.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified including the SwiftUI ownership question the finding turns on. DropsListScreen.swift:20-21 presents `.sheet(item: $sharingDrop) { drop in ShareDropSheet(drop: drop) }` where sharingDrop is a @State GeoDrop VALUE captured at swipe time (:99, :107) — it is never re-derived from library.drops, so ShareDropSheet.swift:6's `let drop` stays the pre-share snapshot for the whole presentation. Tap 1 persists the mutated copy (:200 → DropStore.swift:577-590), the sheet deliberately stays open on a terminal refusal (:160-166), and tap 2 hits the guard at :186-196 which calls library.retrySync(drop) with visibility 'private' (GeoDrop.swift:64 default) and recipientName nil. retrySync (DropStore.swift:537-539) enqueues the caller's snapshot verbatim, and GeoDrop's synthesized encoder always emits the non-optional visibility, so an ack rewrites the server document to 'private' while disk still says 'link' — and under BOTH rule sets the recipient's get then fails the `visibility in ['link','public']` test. B6 fixed the mirror bug and left the API that permits this one. The vacuity note on DropStoreTests.swift:532-554 is correct, and GatedCloudStore records only ids (:842), so no existing test could observe a payload difference.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Make the stale snapshot unrepresentable: `func retrySync(_ id: UUID)` that resolves the row from `drops` and no-ops when absent — exactly the pattern accountDidChange already uses (DropStore.swift:527-529) — with ShareDropSheet passing drop.id. Independently, presentation-captured value types are a recurring hazard in this codebase: have the sheet hold the id and read `library.drops.first { $0.id == dropID } ?? captured` so the caption, the shared copy and the retry all see persisted truth. Extend GatedCloudStore to record saved copies so the regression is testable at all.

verdicts.reasoning: Same defect as seams-5/ux-5, and this lens adds the correct observation that the primed set can only classify events the query raises. Verified: ReactionService.swift:117-120 attaches order(by:'at',desc).limit(to:1) over the client-stamped DropReaction.at (:15), and a limit-1 query produces documentChanges only when the top-1 result set changes, so a later-committing but lower-sorting document raises nothing and :124-131 never runs. The batch observation is also right: when several reactions land in one snapshot the code takes `first(where: .added)` and discards the rest. The closure verdict PARTIAL on flows-4 is the correct call — the watermark is genuinely structural, the query underneath it is not.
verdicts.industrialSolution: As seams-5: server-authoritative ordering field, no limit(1) (or a generous limit with a watermark filter), initial snapshot as the history watermark, and coalesce rather than discard multiple .added changes. Remember the rules key-list and drift-lock update, or the new field turns every reaction into a permission-denied that B1 now escalates to a terminal verdict.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified: ReactionService.swift:121 discards the error parameter (`{ [weak self] snapshot, _ in`) and :122-123 returns silently on nil. Firestore terminates a listener on a permanent error (permission-denied, missing composite index for the order-by, quota) and does not resubscribe — the error is delivered exactly once and the registration is dead. The dead ListenerRegistration stays in `listeners[key]` (assigned at :117), so the re-attach guard at :114 skips it on every re-key, and grep confirms ReactionService.stop() (:154-158) has no production call site, so the dictionary is never cleared for the process lifetime. Nothing is published, so no surface can report it while ReactionOverlay and the share copy keep promising live reactions. The index case is not hypothetical: the toast query needs an index on `at` for the subcollection, and the very first deploy is when that is missing.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Take the error: on non-nil error remove the key from `listeners` and `primedListeners` so the next listenKey change re-attaches, publish `@Published private(set) var listenFailure: String?`, and degrade the 'X sees your reactions' copy when it is set. Extract the callback body into `handleSnapshot(key:snapshot:error:myUid:)` so the failure path is testable without Firestore — the same refactor seams-5's tests need.

verdicts.reasoning: The finding holds; the stated mechanism is half wrong and the correction matters for the fix. Verified code: DropSharingService.swift:49-51 uses getDocument() with the default source and collapses !exists to nil, and ReceiveScreen.swift:127-137 maps BOTH nil and a throw to `failed = true` → 'This drop isn't available / The link may have expired, or you're offline' (:105-117) whose only action is Close, with `.task` (:38-43) running once per presentation so returning connectivity changes nothing. REFUTED as stated: an offline DOCUMENT get with the default source does not return a non-existent snapshot — the SDK raises an error ('Failed to get document because the client is offline', code unavailable) when the snapshot would be !exists && fromCache; the cache-served path applies only to documents already cached. So the SDK already distinguishes absent from unreachable and the app throws that distinction away one layer up. The cache-as-evidence concern is still real for the owner opening their own link (their document IS cached, including their own unflushed delete), which is the seams-4/lens-1 path.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Return the distinction the SDK already gives you: `enum SharedDropFetch { case found(GeoDrop), absentPerServer, unreachable, undecodable }`, mapping a thrown unavailable to .unreachable and a server-sourced !exists to .absentPerServer. Render .unreachable as 'Can't reach the server' with a Retry that re-runs load(), and never blame link expiry for a state you did not observe. Use source:.server for the receive fetch so an owner's cached (possibly locally deleted) copy cannot answer for the server.

ownFindings.title: The incident journal auto-retires on any clean non-empty load, and the `.clean` reap then destroys the round-8 unpushable-writes evidence — a quarantined library ends at "Synced" with no surface ever naming the loss
ownFindings.trace: LocalDropStore.loadDrops:176-181 clears the incident journal whenever a load is clean AND non-empty (`if !drops.isEmpty { clearIncident() }`), and LocalDropStore.save:245-252 calls loadDrops internally, so ANY save rewrites the file with only the successfully decoded rows. Chain A (skipped rows, needs no user action): a partial-decode load journals '3 saved drops couldn't be read (originals kept on disk)' (:167-174) and DropStore.swift:406 publishes it; the next save — including the round-8 B1 ownerUid stamp at DropStore.swift:709, which fires from a background ack with no user involvement — rewrites drops.json without the bad rows; the following load is `.clean` and non-empty, so clearIncident() runs, localReadWarning goes nil, the B4 latch is earned at DropStore.swift:491/:496-497, and the reap at :468-473 (gated only on `.clean`) clears every pendingSyncID whose row is no longer in `drops`, deleting the unpushablePendingCount evidence added this round (:376-378, ProfileScreen.swift:112-122). Chain B (whole-file quarantine): library emptied at DropStore.swift:189-199; the user creates one new drop; that single row makes the next load clean and non-empty, auto-clearing the journal, earning the latch and running the same reap. Final state on both chains: ProfileScreen.swift:146-152 'Synced — the server has confirmed your drops'. Note the reap's own comment (:463-467) argues only about `.absentFile`; a clean load AFTER a quarantine proves nothing about the rows that vanished, but satisfies the guard.
ownFindings.harm: A user whose store is partially or wholly unreadable loses drops permanently, is told once, and is then told the server has confirmed everything. Chain A needs no user action at all — a background cloud ack triggers the rewrite. The round-8 surfaces built to prevent exactly this (the ux-4 problem count and the B4 latch) are erased by the same event that makes the loss permanent, so the honest state is strictly shorter-lived than the loss it describes.
ownFindings.fix: Incidents are acknowledged, never auto-expired: delete the `!drops.isEmpty` auto-clear at LocalDropStore.swift:178-181 and retire the journal only through acknowledgeIncident() (DropStore.swift:209-212), which the user already has an affordance for. Make the reap require positive proof of intentional deletion — key it on a durable deleted-ids record rather than on absence from the current file — and never let a destructive sweep run in the same pass that first observes a clean load after a recorded incident. Stop routing the ownerUid stamp through a whole-file load-modify-write (see lens-5): a single-field update on the local actor removes the background rewrite entirely. Test: journal a skippedRows incident, drive one background ack, assert localReadWarning is still non-nil, hasCompletedCleanRefresh is false, and pendingSyncIDs is unchanged — all three fail today.

ownFindings.title: A refresh superseded during the cloud read throws away local truth it has already loaded, so creating a drop at cold start can leave the library showing only that drop
ownFindings.trace: refresh() loads local rows at DropStore.swift:390 into a LOCAL variable and publishes nothing until `drops = merged` at :436, after the cloud read at :414. Every mutator bumps refreshGeneration (add:544, update:560, remove:594, acknowledgeReadIncident:510), and every post-await guard RETURNS (:391,398,405,408,415,425,427,449). At launch AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:34 starts a refresh; `drops` is still []. If the user taps the create orb and completes a drop during the cloud read (seconds on a cold or offline start, because the Firestore online-state tracker must first decide it is offline), add() inserts into the empty published array (:552-553) and bumps the generation; the refresh then returns at :415 and the already-loaded local rows are discarded. Sent shows one drop, the map shows one drop, and reconcileCloud() (:499) never runs, so no pending write is re-pushed and hasCompletedCleanRefresh stays false. Recovery requires another refresh trigger (DropsListScreen.swift:26 or MapScreen.swift:106). This is the general form of ux-3 (which is the acknowledgeReadIncident special case) and the root of ux-4's false 'saved copy couldn't be read' claim.
ownFindings.harm: A first-time user who creates a drop while the app is still starting sees their existing library vanish from every surface until they happen to visit Explore or pull to refresh; a returning user's queued uploads are not re-pushed for that period. The app is at its most fragile exactly when the user is most likely to act.
ownFindings.fix: Two-phase publish: assign `drops` from the tombstone-suppressed LOCAL set immediately after the local load (right after DropStore.swift:392) and merge cloud rows on top at :436, so a superseded refresh can only lose the cloud half, never local truth. Then make abort mean reschedule, not drop: when a guard fires, set a `refreshNeeded` flag and re-run once the mutation settles (a small debounced coalescing refresh), so no mutator can permanently strand the reconcile. ownFindings.title: Tombstone retirement probes are serialized ahead of the outbox flush and bounded only by a set that (pre-v3) never shrinks — every refresh pays N forced server round-trips before any pending upload is retried
ownFindings.trace: DropStore.swift:446-461 awaits serverConfirmsAbsent once per id in pendingDeleteIDs ∪ unresolvedDeleteIDs, sequentially, each one a getDocument(source:.server) (FirebaseDropStore.swift:162-163) that by contract cannot be answered by the cache; the loop sits BEFORE the reap, before the B4 latch and before reconcileCloud() at :499, which is the only path that re-pushes pending writes and replays pending deletes. Both sets are durable (:816-834) and, under the deployed v2 rules, can never retire (seams-1/lens-3), so they grow monotonically with every delete the user ever makes. The code comment at :445 calls the loop 'bounded by tombstone count' — which is precisely the unbounded quantity. Additionally, any mutator that fires during the loop aborts the refresh at :449, so a long probe loop widens the own-2 window proportionally.
ownFindings.harm: A user who has deleted twenty drops pays twenty forced server reads (billed, battery, radio) on every refresh, forever, and their queued uploads wait behind all of them; with a slow link or a cold start the delay is seconds to tens of seconds before the outbox is even attempted. Post-v3-deploy the set stays small, so the cost collapses — but the ordering (cleanup probes gating user-visible upload progress) remains wrong.
ownFindings.fix: Reorder and bound: run reconcileCloud() (the user's own pending work) BEFORE the retirement probes, cap the probes per pass (e.g. 5 oldest tombstones per refresh, round-robin), and run them concurrently with a task group rather than serially. Give the probe an exponential backoff per id so an id whose probe has failed repeatedly is retried on a slow schedule rather than every refresh, and stop probing entirely once a startup capability probe shows the deployed rules cannot answer absence (see seams-1 fix c). The end-state answer remains the recorded outbox residual, where cleanup is a background queue with its own priority rather than a step inside the read path.

research.shipVerdict:
DO NOT SHIP round 8 as-is against the Wave C charter. The round is a large, real net improvement — B2, B6, seam-1, seam-4, the delete-generation discipline, ux-6's mechanism and B5's drift lock are genuinely closed, and FirestoreAckedTests is the strongest new test asset in the wave — but four charter-class defects remain, three of them created or worsened by round 8 itself.
BLOCKERS. (1) FABRICATED SUCCESS, the charter's own words: 'Synced — the server has confirmed your drops' (ProfileScreen.swift:146-152) is earned by a cache-served getDocuments (FirebaseDropStore.swift:54-56 → DropStore.swift:414-416 → :496-497) with no packet leaving the device; worst case it asserts server confirmation while a drop the user deleted offline is still live and link-readable, because pendingDeleteIDs is deliberately outside the ladder. B4, the round's flagship honesty feature, is satisfiable without a server (ux-1). (2) SILENT DATA LOSS: the state-6 interim fix routes the owner's own link into the generic owner write path, so a fetched pre-edit copy overwrites an unsynced local edit in memory and on disk, is re-uploaded, acked, and reported Synced — and the only user-driven tombstone redemption becomes dead code for a stable account (lens-1/seams-4/flows-1). (3) ALARMING COPY THE MECHANICS CANNOT BACK, the charter inverted: under the rules actually deployed, serverConfirmsAbsent can never answer true, so every offline or never-uploaded delete ends as a permanent 'N deletions couldn't finish — the cloud copy may still exist' at rung 2, masking the unreadable-store warning, the unpushable count, sync errors and upload progress for the life of the install — a state round 7 could heal and round 8 cannot (seams-1/lens-3). (4) THE KEEPSAKE LIES: the Memory recap counts the viewer's own unflushed reaction as landed, directly beneath its own QUEUED badge, on the one artifact the app invites the user to save (ux-2/flows-2).
Add own-1: the incident journal auto-retires on any clean non-empty load and the `.clean` reap then erases the round-8 unpushable-writes count, so a partially destroyed library converges to 'Synced' after a single background ack.
MINIMUM TO SHIP: read provenance (isFromCache) gating every positive claim; an explicit redeem() path with pending-edit protection; the v3 rules deploy made a release gate with the deployed ruleset checked in and the emulator suite run against it, plus never-acked tombstone resolution so the client is not hostage to the rules version; server-sourced, pending-filtered Memory recap; retrySync by id. Those five changes clear all four blockers and eight of the confirmed findings. Everything below them (seams-2, seams-3, ux-3/own-2, lens-2, lens-4, lens-5, lens-6, flows-5) is schedulable within the wave; seams-6, seams-7/lens-7 and seams-8 are hardening and regression locks, not gates.
